entries.name: CB 27/81 — UK FM channels
entries.notes: The UK's own 40-channel FM allocation from 1981, still authorised alongside the CEPT channels below it.

entries.name: 4 m amateur
entries.notes: A Region 1 speciality and the UK has the widest slice of it: 70.450 MHz is the FM calling channel, 70.200 MHz the SSB centre.

entries.name: FM broadcast
entries.notes: The BBC national networks cluster between 88 and 94.6 MHz.

entries.name: DAB — VHF Band III
entries.notes: BBC National DAB on block 12B (225.648 MHz), Digital One on 11D, and a dense layer of local multiplexes.

entries.name: Business radio — simple UK and simple light
entries.notes: Ofcom's shared business channels: taxis, security, events and building sites.

entries.name: UHF television — Freeview
entries.notes: DVB-T2, channels 21–48 after the 700 MHz clearance.

entries.name: Wireless microphones — 863–865 MHz
entries.notes: Licence-exempt radio mics and in-ear monitors, 10 mW ERP.

name: United Kingdom — Ofcom
source: UK Frequency Allocation Table, Issue 22 — curated extract
